en: 2 slices wholegrain bread
60 g ricotta cheese
1 tomato, sliced
1 tsp olive oil
Fresh basil, salt, pepper
Toast the bread slices until crisp
Spread the ricotta generously on each slice
Arrange the tomato slices on top
Finish with basil, oil, salt and pepper
2 eggs
1 small courgette, sliced
Half a bell pepper, chopped
1 tbsp grated parmesan
1 tsp olive oil, salt, pepper
Sauté the courgette and pepper in the oil 4 minutes
Beat the eggs with the parmesan, salt and pepper
Pour the eggs over the vegetables on low heat
Cover 6 minutes until set, then flip for a minute

name.en: Baked Egg and Spinach Cocotte alla Fiorentina

en: 2 eggs and 2 egg whites
Fresh spinach, cooked and drained of water, 100 g
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 20 g
A pinch of nutmeg, salt and black pepper
1 crushed garlic clove (optional)
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with the milk, nutmeg, salt and black pepper.
Add the drained spinach and garlic if desired, mix well.
Pour the mixture into a small oven-safe ramekin, sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake at 180°C for 18-20 minutes until set and golden, serve warm.
Whole-wheat flour 50 g
A pinch of instant yeast and warm water about 30 ml
Honey 1 tsp and softened low-fat butter 1 tsp
A pinch of salt
1 egg (half for the dough, half for brushing)
Light apricot jam 1 tsp for the filling (optional)
Mix the flour with the warm water, yeast, honey, butter, salt and half the egg white until a soft, cohesive dough forms, knead for 5 minutes.
Let the dough rest covered in a warm place 45-60 minutes until doubled in size.
Roll out into a triangle, place the jam at the wide base if desired, roll from the base toward the tip to form a crescent.
Place on a lined tray, brush with the remaining egg, let rest 15 minutes, bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until golden, serve warm.

name.en: Baked Whole Grain Polenta Muffins with Berries

en: Fine cornmeal (polenta) 40 g and whole-wheat flour 20 g
Low-fat milk 80 ml and 1 egg
Baking powder half a tsp and honey 2 tbsp
Mixed fresh berries (blueberries and diced strawberries) 80 g
A pinch of vanilla extract
Grated lemon zest a pinch (optional)
Mix the polenta flour, flour and baking powder in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the milk with the egg, honey, vanilla and lemon zest if desired.
Combine the two mixtures until just combined without overmixing, gently fold in the berries.
Distribute into lined muffin tins, bake at 180°C for 20-22 minutes until golden, serve warm.
2 eggs and 2 egg whites
Fresh mushrooms, sliced, 80 g
Taleggio or low-fat cheese, cut into small cubes, 30 g
Chopped spring onion
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp
Salt, black pepper and chopped chives for garnish (optional)
Brown the mushrooms and spring onion in a dry pan for 4-5 minutes until cooked and the moisture evaporates.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with the milk, salt and black pepper.
Mix the browned mushrooms into the egg mixture, distribute into small lined muffin tins.
Sprinkle the cheese over each, bake at 180°C for 15-18 minutes until set, garnish with chives if desired and serve warm.

name.en: Baked Uova in Purgatorio (Eggs in Purgatory)

en: 2 eggs
Light tomato sauce 150 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and a pinch of red chili flakes
Chopped onion and dried oregano half a tsp
1 tsp olive oil, salt and black pepper
Toasted whole-wheat bread, 1 slice to serve, and chopped parsley for garnish
Brown the onion and garlic in an oven-safe pan for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, chili flakes, oregano, salt and black pepper, cook 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Make two small wells in the sauce, crack an egg into each.
Bake at 190°C for 10-12 minutes until the eggs are cooked to your liking, garnish with parsley and serve with the toasted bread.

name.en: Whole Grain Ciabatta French Toast with Ricotta

en: Whole-wheat ciabatta bread, cut into slices, 2 slices (70 g)
1 egg and 1 egg white
Low-fat milk 60 ml and a pinch of vanilla extract
Low-fat ricotta cheese 40 g
Honey 1 tbsp and a pinch of ground cinnamon
Fresh berries to serve (optional)
Whisk the egg and egg white with the milk and vanilla in a shallow bowl.
Dip the bread slices in the mixture on both sides until soaked without falling apart.
Bake at 200°C for 12-15 minutes on each side until golden.
Mix the ricotta with the honey and cinnamon, spread over the toast and serve with fresh berries if desired.
Thin whole-wheat pastry sheet, 1 piece (50 g)
2 eggs and 1 egg white
Fresh spinach, cooked and drained, 100 g
Red bell pepper, diced, 50 g
Low-fat grated cheese 30 g
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp, salt and black pepper
Roll out the pastry into a small lined tart tin.
Whisk the eggs and egg white with the milk, salt and black pepper.
Add the spinach and bell pepper, pour the mixture over the pastry, sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake at 190°C for 25-30 minutes until the filling sets and the pastry turns golden, let cool slightly before slicing.

name.en: Whole Grain Ricotta and Honey Pancakes

en: Whole-wheat flour 50 g and baking powder half a tsp
Low-fat ricotta cheese 60 g
1 egg and low-fat milk 60 ml
Honey 2 tbsp and a pinch of vanilla extract
Grated lemon zest a pinch (optional)
Fresh berries and extra honey to serve
Mix the flour and baking powder in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the ricotta with the egg, milk, honey, vanilla and lemon zest if desired.
Combine the two mixtures gently without overmixing.
Pour a tablespoon of batter into a hot non-stick pan for each pancake, cook 2-3 minutes on each side until golden, serve with berries and honey.
100 g wholewheat pasta
4 ripe tomatoes, peeled
2 garlic cloves
1 tbsp olive oil
Fresh basil, salt, pepper
Heat the oil and soften the garlic without browning it
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes
Boil the pasta until al dente
Toss with the sauce, 2 tbsp pasta water and basil
Half cup cooked cannellini beans
1 carrot, 1 celery stick, 1 onion, diced
2 tomatoes, chopped
30 g small pasta
1 tbsp olive oil, basil, salt
Sauté the onion, carrot and celery in the oil 5 minutes
Add the tomatoes and 4 cups of water, bring to a boil
Add the beans and simmer 15 minutes
Add the pasta, cook until tender, finish with basil

name.en: Baked Chicken and Vegetable Risotto Leggero

en: Arborio rice or regular rice 70 g, uncooked
Chicken breast, cut into small pieces, 100 g
Zucchini and carrot, diced, 150 g total
Chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Light chicken stock 400 ml
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 20 g
Brown the chicken in a dry pot for 4-5 minutes until golden, set aside.
In the same pot, brown the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, add the rice and stir for a minute.
Add the stock gradually, one ladle at a time while stirring constantly, add the zucchini and carrot halfway through, continue until the rice is cooked (18-20 minutes total).
Return the chicken to the pot in the final minutes until fully cooked, add the cheese and stir, serve hot.

name.en: Pasta e Fagioli (Pasta and Bean Soup)

en: Canned white beans, drained, 150 g
Small whole-wheat pasta 50 g
Diced tomato, chopped onion and diced carrot
2 crushed garlic cloves and dried oregano half a tsp
Light vegetable stock 500 ml
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese to serve
Brown the onion, garlic and carrot in a dry pot for 4-5 minutes.
Add the tomato and oregano, cook 3 minutes.
Add the stock, cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and beans, cook 10-12 more minutes until the pasta is cooked, serve hot with the cheese.

name.en: Baked Orzo with Chicken and Spinach

en: Whole-wheat orzo pasta 70 g
Chicken breast, cut into small pieces, 100 g
Fresh spinach 100 g
Diced tomato, chopped onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
Light chicken stock 400 ml
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 20 g
Brown the chicken in a dry pot for 4-5 minutes until golden, set aside.
In the same pot, brown the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, add the tomato and cook 2 minutes.
Add the orzo and stock, cover and simmer 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the orzo is cooked.
Return the chicken to the pot with the spinach, cook 3-4 more minutes until the spinach wilts and the chicken is fully cooked, add the cheese and serve hot.
Canned white beans, drained and partially mashed, 150 g
Slightly stale whole-wheat bread, cubed, 50 g
Black cabbage (cavolo nero) or kale, cut into strips, 100 g
Carrot and celery, diced, and diced tomato, 150 g total
Chopped onion and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Light vegetable stock 500 ml
Brown the onion, garlic, carrot and celery in a dry pot for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato and black cabbage, cook 3 minutes until wilted.
Add the mashed beans and stock, cover and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the bread cubes, cook 5 more minutes until they absorb the soup, let sit 5 minutes before serving to thicken the texture.

name.en: Baked Farro Salad with Roasted Vegetables

en: Farro grain (or whole wheat berries) 70 g, uncooked
Bell pepper, zucchini and eggplant, diced, 200 g total
1 crushed garlic clove and dried oregano half a tsp
1 tsp olive oil and lemon juice 1 tbsp
Low-fat feta cheese, crumbled, 30 g
Chopped fresh basil, salt and black pepper
Boil the farro grain according to package instructions until cooked (usually 20-25 minutes), drain.
Mix the diced vegetables with the garlic, oregano, oil, salt and black pepper.
Spread on a lined tray, roast in the oven at 220°C for 18-20 minutes until cooked and lightly charred at the edges.
Mix the cooked farro with the roasted vegetables, lemon juice and basil, sprinkle with the feta and serve warm or cold.
Light chicken stock 400 ml
2 eggs and 1 egg white
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 30 g
Chopped fresh spinach 80 g
A pinch of nutmeg, salt and black pepper
Chopped fresh parsley for garnish (optional)
Heat the stock in a medium pot until boiling.
Whisk the eggs and egg white with the cheese and nutmeg in a bowl.
Add the spinach to the boiling stock, cook 2 minutes until wilted.
Lower the heat slightly, pour the egg mixture gradually while stirring constantly with a fork until thin ribbons form, season with salt and black pepper, garnish with parsley and serve hot.
Eggplant, cut into slices, 250 g
Light tomato sauce 200 g
Low-fat mozzarella cheese, grated, 50 g
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 20 g
Chopped fresh basil and 1 crushed garlic clove
Salt, black pepper and a light spray of olive oil
Spray the eggplant slices lightly with oil, arrange on a lined tray.
Bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until softened and lightly charred at the edges.
Mix the tomato sauce with the garlic and basil, layer the eggplant slices in a small oven-safe dish, pour a layer of sauce, repeat the layers.
Sprinkle the mozzarella and parmesan over the final layer, bake 18-20 more minutes until the cheese melts and browns, serve hot.
Whole-wheat meat or cheese-filled tortellini (store-bought) 150 g
Light chicken stock 400 ml
Carrot and celery, diced small, 100 g total
Chopped onion
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese to serve
Chopped fresh parsley for garnish, salt and black pepper
Brown the onion, carrot and celery in a dry pot for 5 minutes.
Add the stock, cover and simmer 10 minutes until the vegetables are cooked.
Add the tortellini, cook according to package instructions (usually 5-7 minutes) until cooked.
Season with salt and black pepper, serve hot with the parmesan and parsley.
170 g skinless chicken
1 onion and 1 bell pepper, sliced
3 tomatoes, chopped
50 g mushrooms, sliced
1 tbsp olive oil, oregano, bay leaf
Brown the chicken in the oil on both sides and set aside
Sauté the onion, pepper and mushrooms in the same pan
Add the tomatoes and herbs, cook 5 minutes
Return the chicken, cover and simmer 25 minutes
150 g salmon fillet
Half a lemon (juice and zest)
1 garlic clove, crushed
1 tbsp olive oil
Courgette, cherry tomatoes, rosemary, salt
Mix the oil, lemon, garlic and rosemary
Marinate the salmon for 15 minutes
Spread the vegetables in a tray and place the salmon on top
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes
Thin turkey breast slices 140 g
Low-fat prosciutto, 2 thin slices
Fresh sage leaves, 4 leaves
Lemon juice 1 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil
1 crushed garlic clove and dry white wine 1 tbsp (alcohol cooks off during cooking, optional)
A little salt and black pepper
Place a sage leaf on each turkey slice, cover with a slice of prosciutto, secure with a toothpick if needed.
Season with salt and black pepper on the other side.
Brown in an oven-safe pan for 2-3 minutes on the prosciutto side until crisp, flip.
Add the garlic, wine and lemon juice, bake at 200°C for 10-12 minutes until fully cooked, serve hot.
Cod fillet 140 g
Diced tomato and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Pitted black olives, halved, 1 tbsp
Drained capers 1 tsp (optional)
Chopped fresh parsley and dried oregano half a tsp
1 tsp olive oil, salt and black pepper
Brown the garlic in a dry pan for one minute.
Add the tomato and oregano, cook 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the olives and capers, cook 2 minutes.
Arrange the fish fillet on a lined baking tray, pour the sauce over it, sprinkle with the oil, salt and black pepper, bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until cooked, garnish with parsley and serve hot.
Chicken breast, pounded thin, 140 g
Whole-wheat breadcrumbs 40 g
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 1 tbsp
Egg white for coating
Dried oregano half a tsp, salt and black pepper
Lemon juice and arugula leaves to serve
Season the chicken with salt and black pepper.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the cheese and oregano.
Dip the chicken in the egg white then in the breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp, serve with lemon juice and arugula.
Whole-wheat linguine pasta 70 g, uncooked
Medium shrimp, peeled, 140 g
Zucchini, cut into thin ribbons (julienne), 150 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and a pinch of red chili flakes
Lemon juice 1 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil
Chopped fresh parsley, salt and black pepper
Boil the pasta according to package instructions until slightly firm (10-12 minutes), reserve a cup of the cooking water.
Brown the garlic and red chili flakes in a dry pan for one minute.
Add the shrimp and cook 2-3 minutes until they change colour, add the zucchini and cook 2 minutes.
Add the drained pasta with a little of the cooking water, lemon juice and oil, toss until combined, garnish with parsley, salt and black pepper and serve hot.
Lean veal shank (osso buco) 160 g
Diced tomato and diced carrot and celery, 200 g total
Chopped onion and 2 crushed garlic cloves
Dry white wine 2 tbsp (alcohol cooks off during cooking, optional)
Light meat stock 150 ml and grated lemon zest a pinch
Chopped fresh parsley and 1 crushed garlic clove for garnish (gremolata)
Brown the veal in an oven-safe pot for 4-5 minutes on each side until golden, set aside.
In the same pot, brown the onion, garlic, carrot and celery for 5 minutes.
Add the wine if desired and let it evaporate for a minute, add the tomato and stock.
Return the veal to the pot, cover and bake at 160°C for 50-60 minutes until very tender, mix the parsley, garlic and lemon zest for the gremolata and sprinkle over the dish before serving.
Branzino fillet or similar white fish 140 g
Cherry tomatoes, halved, and pitted green olives, 100 g total
1 crushed garlic clove and a little fresh thyme
Lemon juice 2 tbsp and 1 tsp olive oil
Salt and black pepper
Baking paper for wrapping
Spread a large piece of baking paper on the work surface.
Arrange the cherry tomatoes and olives in the centre, place the fish fillet on top.
Mix the garlic, lemon juice, oil, salt and black pepper, pour over the fish, sprinkle with thyme.
Fold the paper tightly into a sealed parcel, bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, open carefully when serving.
Chicken breast, pounded thin, 140 g
Whole-wheat flour 1 tbsp for coating
Fresh lemon juice 2 tbsp and grated lemon zest a pinch
Drained capers 1 tsp
Light chicken stock 100 ml and 1 crushed garlic clove
Chopped fresh parsley for garnish, salt and black pepper
Season the chicken with salt and black pepper, coat with a thin layer of flour.
Arrange in a small oven-safe dish.
Mix the stock, lemon juice, zest, garlic and capers, pour over the chicken.
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until fully cooked, garnish with parsley and serve hot.
Swordfish fillet or similar white fish 140 g
Diced tomato and chopped onion
Pitted green olives, halved, and drained capers, 1 tbsp total
1 crushed garlic clove and dried oregano half a tsp
Raisins 1 tsp and toasted pine nuts 1 tsp (optional)
1 tsp olive oil, salt and black pepper
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pan for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato and oregano, cook 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the olives, capers, raisins and pine nuts if desired, cook 2 minutes.
Arrange the fish fillet on a lined baking tray, pour the sauce over it, sprinkle with the oil, salt and black pepper, bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until cooked, serve hot.
50 g fresh mozzarella
6 cherry tomatoes
Fresh basil leaves
1 tsp olive oil
Salt and black pepper
Halve the mozzarella and the tomatoes
Arrange them alternately on a plate
Tuck a basil leaf between each pair
Drizzle with oil, season and serve at once
2 slices rustic bread
2 tomatoes, finely diced
1 garlic clove
1 tsp olive oil
Basil, salt, balsamic vinegar
Mix the tomatoes with basil, salt and oil
Let them sit 10 minutes so the flavours mingle
Toast the bread and rub the surface with the garlic clove
Spoon the tomato mix on top and drizzle the vinegar
Zucchini, cut into very thin lengthwise slices, 4 slices (150 g)
Low-fat ricotta cheese 60 g
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 1 tbsp
Chopped fresh basil and 1 small crushed garlic clove
Light tomato sauce 60 g
Salt and black pepper
Grill the zucchini slices in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes on each side until slightly softened.
Mix the ricotta, parmesan, basil, garlic, salt and black pepper.
Place a small spoonful of filling at one end of each zucchini slice and roll tightly.
Arrange in a small oven-safe dish seam-side down, pour the tomato sauce over them, bake at 190°C for 15-18 minutes until cooked, serve warm.
Whole-wheat baguette, cut into thin slices, 3 slices (45 g)
Canned white beans, drained and partially mashed, 80 g
1 crushed garlic clove and lemon juice 1 tsp
Chopped fresh basil and a little chopped rosemary
1 tsp olive oil, salt and black pepper
Cherry tomatoes, halved, for garnish (optional)
Bake the bread slices in the oven at 180°C for 8-10 minutes until crisp.
Mix the mashed beans with the garlic, lemon juice, basil, rosemary, oil, salt and black pepper.
Spread the bean mixture on each toasted bread slice.
Garnish with cherry tomatoes if desired and serve immediately.
Eggplant, cut into thin lengthwise slices, 4 slices (150 g)
Low-fat ricotta cheese 60 g
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 1 tbsp
Chopped fresh basil and 1 small crushed garlic clove
Light tomato sauce 60 g
Salt and black pepper
Grill the eggplant slices in a dry pan for 2-3 minutes on each side until softened.
Mix the ricotta, parmesan, basil, garlic, salt and black pepper.
Place a small spoonful of filling at one end of each eggplant slice and roll tightly.
Arrange in a small oven-safe dish seam-side down, pour the tomato sauce over them, bake at 190°C for 15-18 minutes until cooked, serve warm.

name.en: Marinated Olives and Roasted Pepper Antipasto Cups

en: Mixed green and black olives 60 g
Roasted red bell pepper, cut into strips, 50 g
1 crushed garlic clove and dried oregano half a tsp
1 tsp olive oil
A little lemon juice
Chopped parsley for garnish (optional)
Mix the olives and roasted bell pepper in a bowl.
Add the garlic, oregano, oil and lemon juice, stir gently.
Let the flavours infuse in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.
Distribute into serving cups, garnish with parsley if desired and serve at room temperature.

name.en: Baked Whole Grain Grissini with Rosemary

en: Whole-wheat flour 60 g
A pinch of instant yeast and warm water about 40 ml
1 tsp olive oil and a pinch of salt
Chopped fresh rosemary 1 tsp
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 1 tsp (optional)
Sesame seeds for garnish (optional)
Mix the flour with the warm water, yeast, oil, salt and rosemary until a soft, cohesive dough forms, knead for 5 minutes.
Let the dough rest covered in a warm place 45-60 minutes until doubled in size.
Divide the dough into 6 equal pieces, roll each with your hands into long thin sticks.
Arrange on a lined tray, sprinkle with cheese and sesame seeds if desired, bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until golden and crisp.
Large mushrooms (small portobello), stems removed, 4 pieces (150 g)
Chopped mushroom stems and chopped fresh spinach, 60 g total
1 crushed garlic clove and low-fat ricotta cheese 40 g
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 1 tbsp
Whole-wheat breadcrumbs 1 tbsp
Salt, black pepper and chopped fresh basil for garnish (optional)
Brown the chopped mushroom stems, spinach and garlic in a dry pan for 4 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Mix with the ricotta, parmesan, salt and black pepper.
Stuff the mushrooms with the mixture, sprinkle with the breadcrumbs.
Arrange on a lined tray, bake at 190°C for 18-20 minutes until cooked and golden, garnish with basil if desired and serve warm.
Coarse cornmeal (polenta) 50 g
Water or light vegetable stock 200 ml
Chopped chives and chopped rosemary 1 tsp total
Low-fat grated parmesan cheese 1 tbsp
A light spray of olive oil, salt and black pepper
Light tomato sauce to serve (optional)
Boil the water or stock in a medium pot.
Gradually add the polenta flour while stirring constantly, cook 5-7 minutes until the texture thickens.
Add the herbs, cheese, salt and black pepper, pour the mixture into a lined flat tray about 1.5 cm thick and let it cool and set for at least 30 minutes (or in the fridge to set faster).
Cut into sticks, spray lightly with oil, bake at 220°C for 20-25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp, serve with tomato sauce if desired.
Eggplant, cut into small cubes, 150 g
Diced tomato, chopped onion and diced celery
Pitted green olives, halved, and drained capers, 1 tbsp total
Apple cider vinegar 1 tsp and honey half a tsp
1 tsp olive oil, salt and black pepper
Chopped fresh basil for garnish
Brown the eggplant cubes in a dry pan for 6-8 minutes until softened and charred at the edges.
Add the tomato, onion and celery, cook 4 minutes.
Add the olives, capers, vinegar, honey, salt and black pepper, cook 3 more minutes until the flavours meld.
Distribute into serving cups, garnish with basil and serve warm or cold.
80 g ricotta cheese
1 tsp honey
A pinch of lemon zest
A handful of berries and strawberries
1 tsp crushed pistachios
Whip the ricotta with the honey until smooth
Stir in the lemon zest
Spoon into a cup and top with the berries
Sprinkle the pistachios and serve chilled
100 g Greek yogurt, lightly frozen
1 hot espresso shot
1 tsp honey
A dusting of raw cocoa
Crushed hazelnuts (optional)
Mix the yogurt with the honey and freeze 30 minutes
Brew the espresso hot
Put the yogurt in a cup and pour the coffee over it
Dust with cocoa, add hazelnuts and serve at once
Low-fat milk 200 ml
Low-fat Greek yogurt 60 g
Powdered gelatine half a tsp
Honey 2 tbsp
Vanilla extract 1 tsp
Fresh berries for garnish (optional)
Soak the gelatine in 2 tbsp cold water for 5 minutes until softened.
Heat the milk with the honey in a small pot until nearly boiling, remove from heat and add the soaked gelatine, stir until fully dissolved.
Add the vanilla and yogurt, mix well until the texture is smooth.
Pour into serving cups and chill in the fridge for at least 4 hours, garnish with fresh berries if desired and serve cold.

name.en: Baked Apple and Cinnamon Crostata Leggera

en: Thin whole-wheat pastry sheet, 1 piece (50 g)
Apple, sliced thin, 150 g
Ground cinnamon half a tsp and lemon juice 1 tsp
Brown sugar 2 tbsp
Melted low-fat butter 1 tsp
Light apricot jam 1 tsp for glazing (optional)
Mix the apple slices with the lemon juice and cinnamon.
Roll out the pastry on a lined tray.
Arrange the apple slices in the centre, leaving a 3-4 cm border, sprinkle with the brown sugar.
Fold the border inward loosely, brush the edge with melted butter, bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until the edges are golden, brush with warm apricot jam if desired and serve warm.
Low-fat mascarpone cheese or low-fat Greek yogurt 80 g
Cold espresso coffee 60 ml (decaf optional)
Whole-wheat ladyfinger biscuits, 2 pieces
Unsweetened raw cocoa powder for dusting 1 tsp
Honey 2 tbsp
A pinch of vanilla extract
Mix the mascarpone with the honey and vanilla until the texture is combined.
Quickly dip the ladyfinger biscuits in the cold coffee (don't leave them too long so they don't crumble), arrange in the bottom of the serving cup.
Spread half the mascarpone mixture over it, repeat with another layer of biscuit and mixture.
Dust the top of the cup with cocoa, chill in the fridge for at least 2 hours before serving.

name.en: Baked Pear and Amaretti Crumble Leggero

en: Pear, diced, 150 g
Lemon juice 1 tsp and a pinch of ground cinnamon
Coarsely crushed amaretti biscuits 20 g
Whole-wheat flour 2 tbsp
Oats 1 tbsp and brown sugar 1 tbsp
Cold low-fat butter, cubed, 1 tsp
Mix the diced pear with the lemon juice and cinnamon, distribute into a small oven-safe cup.
Mix the crushed amaretti biscuits with the flour, oats and brown sugar.
Rub the cold butter into the dry mixture with your fingertips until coarse crumbs form.
Sprinkle the crumb over the pear, bake at 190°C for 25-30 minutes until golden and the pear is cooked, serve warm.
1 egg yolk and 1 whole egg
Honey 2 tbsp
Low-fat milk 100 ml
Vanilla extract 1 tsp (a substitute for the traditional sweet wine)
A pinch of ground cinnamon
Fresh berries to serve (optional)
Whisk the whole egg and yolk with the honey in a heatproof bowl until the mixture lightens in colour.
Place the bowl over a pot of gently simmering water (double boiler) without the bowl touching the water.
Gradually add the milk and vanilla while whisking constantly for 8-10 minutes until the mixture thickens and becomes foamy.
Pour into serving cups immediately, sprinkle with cinnamon and serve warm with fresh berries if desired.

name.en: Baked Fig and Ricotta Tart Leggera

en: Thin whole-wheat pastry sheet, 1 piece (50 g)
Low-fat ricotta cheese 80 g
Fresh figs, quartered, 3 pieces (100 g)
Honey 2 tbsp and a pinch of vanilla extract
A pinch of ground cinnamon
Coarsely chopped walnuts 1 tsp for garnish (optional)
Roll out the pastry into a small lined tart tin.
Mix the ricotta with the honey, vanilla and cinnamon until combined, spread over the pastry.
Arrange the fig quarters over the ricotta mixture.
Bake at 190°C for 25-28 minutes until the edges are golden, sprinkle with walnuts if desired and serve warm.
Low-fat ricotta cheese 100 g
Unsweetened raw cocoa powder 2 tbsp
Honey 2 tbsp and a pinch of vanilla extract
Low-fat milk 2 tbsp
A pinch of ground cinnamon (optional)
Fresh berries or a few dark chocolate shavings for garnish (optional)
Mix the ricotta with the cocoa, honey, vanilla and milk in a bowl until the texture is completely smooth.
Add the cinnamon if desired and stir.
Distribute the mousse into small serving cups.
Chill in the fridge for at least an hour, garnish with berries or chocolate shavings if desired and serve cold.

name.en: Baked Sicilian Orange and Almond Cake Leggero

en: Ground almonds 50 g and whole-wheat flour 20 g
Fresh orange juice 60 ml and grated orange zest 1 tsp
1 egg and 1 egg white
Honey 2 tbsp and baking powder half a tsp
A pinch of vanilla extract
Thin orange slices for garnish (optional)
Whisk the egg and egg white with the honey until slightly foamy.
Add the orange juice, zest and vanilla, mix well.
Add the ground almonds, flour and baking powder, gently fold until the texture is combined.
Pour into a small oven-safe dish lined with baking paper, garnish the top with orange slices if desired, bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until golden and set, let cool before slicing.
